# PMP 10-Week Study Plan for Weekday-Only Study

A steady plan with short weekday sessions works well for PMP prep, especially with 3 years of coordination experience. This version uses **6 hours per week**, keeps sessions short, and includes **built-in review weeks** to reinforce retention.

## Week-by-Week PMP Roadmap

| Week | Focus | Topic Priorities | Practice Question Target | Weekly Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PMP setup + exam structure | Exam domains; PMBOK mindset; ECO overview; agile vs predictive | 50 questions | Understand the exam format and build a study routine |
| 2 | People domain basics | Leadership styles; team development; conflict resolution; stakeholder engagement | 60 questions | Strengthen people-focused decision making |
| 3 | Process domain planning | Scope; schedule; cost; quality; risk; procurement; communications | 70 questions | Connect planning processes to real project situations |
| 4 | Process domain execution + monitoring | Change control; issue management; earned value basics; performance reporting | 70 questions | Improve response selection for project control scenarios |
| 5 | Agile and hybrid methods | Scrum basics; servant leadership; backlog; iterative delivery; hybrid tailoring | 80 questions | Recognize agile and hybrid cues quickly |
| 6 | Review week 1 | Revisit weak areas from Weeks 1–5; mixed-domain recall; formula refresh | 100 questions mixed | Consolidate core concepts and reduce knowledge gaps |
| 7 | Advanced scenario practice | Situational judgment; conflict; risk response; stakeholder trade-offs; team coaching | 90 questions | Build exam-style reasoning and eliminate distractors |
| 8 | Review week 2 | Full-domain recap; process interactions; agile/predictive comparison; memory drills | 120 questions mixed | Improve speed, accuracy, and concept retention |
| 9 | Full mock exam week | Timed practice; endurance; review incorrect answers; pacing strategy | 180 questions total | Simulate exam conditions and identify final weak spots |
| 10 | Final revision + confidence week | High-yield notes; formulas; agile mindset; common traps; light practice | 60 questions early in week | Enter exam week calm, focused, and well-rehearsed |

## Weekly Study Structure by Short Sessions

Each week uses **5 weekday sessions of about 70–75 minutes** to total 6 hours.

- **Monday:** New concept 1
- **Tuesday:** New concept 2
- **Wednesday:** Short recap + 20–25 practice questions
- **Thursday:** New concept 3 or scenario practice
- **Friday:** Review mistakes + 25–30 practice questions

### Suggested session format
- 10 min: quick recap of prior notes
- 35 min: new content
- 20 min: practice questions
- 10 min: error review and flashcards

## Final 3-Day Revision Schedule

### Day 1: Core Concepts Reset
- Review PMP domains, process groups, and agile vs predictive differences
- Re-read summary notes for scope, schedule, cost, risk, and stakeholder topics
- Do 25–30 mixed questions
- Focus on why the correct answer is best, not just on memorizing terms

### Day 2: Scenario and Weak-Area Repair
- Review missed questions from mock exams
- Revisit conflict resolution, change control, servant leadership, and risk response
- Do 25–30 scenario-based questions
- Build a one-page “last look” sheet of traps and reminders

### Day 3: Light Refresh + Exam Readiness
- Review formulas, key terms, and agile ceremonies
- Do 10–15 easy warm-up questions only
- Stop heavy study early; prioritize sleep, timing, and calm pacing
- Prepare exam logistics and test-day materials

## Study Priorities for Best Results

- **Highest priority:** People domain, scenario judgment, and agile/hybrid decision making
- **Second priority:** Process interactions, change control, and planning/execution flow
- **Third priority:** Formula basics, terminology, and memorization-heavy details
- **Best strategy for your background:** Use your coordination experience to anchor answers in real project behavior, then align those instincts with PMP wording

## Quick Actions
